compiled_prompt:
[TASK: ARCHITECTURAL RELIGHTING & STATIC RECONSTRUCTION]
Transform the reference photogrammetry plate into a razor-sharp, photorealistic architectural image.
Keep the reference plate's exact composition: every edge, horizon line, and object position stays where it is.

MANDATORY TRANSFORMATION RULES:
1. PLANAR RECTIFICATION & GEOMETRY LOCK: Treat the reference image as an immutable spatial coordinate frame. Eliminate all 3D mesh polygon wobble, melted facades, and distorted rooflines. Plumb all vertical walls to true gravity vertical. Render the specific materials, coursing, window types, and roof forms named in the SCENE section below with sharp, correct detail.
2. STATIC DECLUTTERING (MANDATORY): COMPLETELY ERASE all transient vehicles, parked cars, delivery vans, pedestrians, and temporary street clutter from the seed image. Repaint the ground plane with the authentic surfacing, kerbs, and pavement named in the SCENE section below.
3. BOTANICAL PHENOLOGY & CANOPY INTEGRITY: Overwrite all raw 3D mesh blob foliage with authentic seasonal canopy structures matching the target date. Zero green summer foliage during dormant/autumn/winter periods:
   - Temporal Target: 23 September (Early Autumn).
- Species Composition: *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime), *Aesculus hippocastanum* (Horse Chestnut), and *Betula pendula* (Silver Birch).
- Canopy Phenology: Dense, high-volume mature canopies entering early autumn senescence; *Tilia × europaea* displaying pale yellow marginal chlorosis;
4. OPTICAL DEPTH: Sharp focus across the entire frame, near to far. No blur, no depth-of-field falloff, no vignetting.

[SOLAR & ATMOSPHERIC LIGHTING OVERRIDE]
SOLAR RELIGHTING DIRECTIVE (4500K Late afternoon raking sunlight with warm golden highlights):
- SUN POSITION IN SCREEN SPACE: Sun is directly ahead of the camera in the centre background (True Azimuth 244.1°, Elevation 16.7°).
- FACADE ILLUMINATION: all camera-facing facades are in shadow, reading as backlit silhouettes with a bright rim along their sunward edges; left- and right-facing walls are lit roughly equally.
- CAST SHADOW DIRECTION: cast shadows project directly toward the camera, down the frame.
- CAST SHADOW LENGTH: Every cast shadow is 3.3 times as long as the height of the object casting it. A 100 m tower casts a 334 m shadow. Apply this ratio to every object in the scene.
- SHADOW OVERWRITE RULE: MANDATORY: Erase every cast shadow present in the reference plate before relighting. Render all previously shadowed ground and facades as if that shadow never existed, then cast entirely new shadows so that cast shadows project directly toward the camera, down the frame. Every shadow must be angled toward the RIGHT; a shadow running straight up or straight down the frame is wrong. Do not retain, tint, or reuse any shadow from the reference plate.
- WEATHER/SKY: Crisp clear sky with direct solar exposure.

[SCENE GEOMETRY & AUTHENTIC LITHICS]
West Register House terminated along Charlotte Square axis: monumental Neoclassical Craigleith sandstone ashlar facade with central tetrastyle colossal portico, triangular pediment, rusticated ground-level arcade, flanked by two-storey pavilion wings with channelled masonry. Rising above, a tall cylindrical drum with paired Corinthian pilasters and arched fenestration, supporting a ribbed hemispherical dome sheathed in verdigris-oxidized copper with lead roll joints and a crowning cupola lantern. Flanking unified Georgian palace-front terraces of polished buff sandstone ashlar, featuring three storeys over rusticated basements, Scottish Ballachulish slate roofs, rectilinear parapets, rhythmically set ashlar chimneystacks with ceramic pots, and recessed 6-over-6 timber sash-and-case windows with painted timber glazing bars. Centered in foreground parkland, the Prince Albert Memorial: a patinated bronze equestrian statue atop a stepped, polished pink Peterhead granite and sandstone plinth with bronze bas-relief panels. Park interior composed of clipped Lolium perenne and Poa pratensis lawn bordered by cast-iron spearhead railings.
